description: Card P's targets for "6.7 L straight-six turbo diesel pickup": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 6/2, 37.5 Hz at the 750 rpm idle and 160 Hz at the 3199 rpm limiter.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a rev limiter holds the speed within a few percent of where it cuts (some 100 to 200 rpm at 6500)

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor at least 3 m/s in ten seconds)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 6690 cc; 38 to 47 kW a litre

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 6690 cc: 2700 to 3100 rpm

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 6690 cc; BMEP 18.8 to 27.6 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2)

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 6690 cc: 1500 to 1900 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span)

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 650 to 800 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 750

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb); a lope of more than 150 rpm over the range's top is a fault

targets.name: Boost at its target
targets.source: the build's own target (2.00 bar); a wastegate or vane loop holds a steady full load within some 0.1 bar of its target once spooled (makers' boost-control tolerances; judgement)

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: the gas at a diesel's exhaust valve at full load, before the port and pipe cool it: some 850 to 1100 K (judgement: the header's 700 to 950 K, below, plus the port's cooling; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14)

targets.name: Header gas at full load
targets.source: a thermocouple a little way down a diesel's manifold reads some 700 to 950 K at full load (makers' pre-turbine limits near 1000 K; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14)

targets.name: Quarter mile: time
targets.source: Hale's rule, ET = 5.825 (lb/hp)^(1/3) s, with the kind's published power (285 kW) and the build's mass: 15.71 s; 5 % quicker to 15 % slower for street tyres and an automatic's launch (card I's test holds drag radials to 8 %)

targets.name: Quarter mile: trap speed
targets.source: Hale's rule, trap = 234 (hp/lb)^(1/3) mph: 38.8 m/s (140 km/h), within 8 % under to 6 % over

targets.name: Top speed
targets.source: the redline in top gear with the build's gearing: 228 km/h, within 7 % (geared, not drag-limited); no speed governor is simulated
